idiom_name: async step list carried on the envelope + for/await dispatcher, step names in a registry
implementation_notes: JavaScript's first-class async functions make the itinerary an array of steps on the envelope (async (body) => body) plus a cursor, applied with a while/for-await loop; Array.prototype.reduce composes the same list into a single function when no progress marker is needed, which is why the classic Router/Step object graph simply disappears. Koa/Express middleware chains are the language's canonical stage composition, but their order is fixed at startup; Node's stream.pipeline is the same idea for byte streams, so both serve as cousins rather than implementations. Because functions cannot cross a queue, distributed slips carry step names and the registry resolves them.
pitfalls: An unhandled rejection aborts the chain after earlier steps have already had side effects: catch per step and decide retry versus compensation explicitly.
Closures capture sockets, DB handles and request state - a slip that is stored (DLQ, retry queue, cache) and resumed later holds stale resources.
Shallow-copying envelopes or forgetting to advance the cursor makes retries repeat steps and duplicates non-idempotent work; concurrent steps must not share one envelope object.
